title: Project Helix release metadata
description: A write-once record of one release candidate and the review gates it passed. Identified by commit_sha, which is immutable: an approval recorded against a SHA always refers to the exact version of the code that was reviewed. See docs/RELEASE_METADATA.md.

pull_request.description: Number of the pull request that introduced this commit.

commit_sha.description: Full 40-character lowercase hex SHA of the reviewed commit. IMMUTABLE: this field identifies the record and must never be changed after the record is written. A short SHA, branch name, or tag is not acceptable, because those can resolve to different code over time.

developer.description: GitHub login of the author of the change.

human_reviewer.description: GitHub login of the human who approved the pull request. Must differ from developer: self-review does not satisfy the peer-approval gate.

test_status.description: Conclusion of the automated test gate for this commit. Set from the check-run conclusion, never asserted by hand.

security_review_status.description: Outcome of the security gate: the security-check workflow together with the AI security review. When set to 'waived', this schema additionally requires waiver_authorized_by, waiver_reason and waiver_timestamp, so a waiver can never be recorded anonymously or without a reason.

staging_url.description: Base URL where this commit was deployed and verified on staging. Null only if it has not been deployed to staging yet; a release promoted to production with a null staging_url was never verified.

business_approval_required.description: Whether this release requires executive/business sign-off before production, beyond technical peer approval. Enforced operationally by the required-reviewer rule on the production GitHub Environment, not by this field.

rollback_safe.description: Whether the previously deployed version can be redeployed over this release without data loss or breakage. Defaults to false: rollback is never assumed safe until a project's actual deployment implementation demonstrably supports it. Must be false for destructive or non-backward-compatible migrations and one-way data backfills. The rollback workflow refuses to run when this is false.

database_migration.description: Whether this release adds, alters, or drops database schema, or backfills data.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when this record was written. Records the moment of the release decision, not the commit date. The pattern is enforced alongside 'format' on purpose: most validators treat 'format' as an annotation only unless an optional library is installed, so 'format' alone would accept arbitrary text here.

waiver_authorized_by.description: GitHub login of the Technical Admin who authorized the security-review waiver. Required only when security_review_status is 'waived', and forbidden otherwise. ONLY a Technical Admin may authorize a waiver; this schema records who did, but cannot verify that they hold that role — see docs/RELEASE_METADATA.md.

waiver_reason.description: Why the security gate was waived for this release, and what compensating control applies. Required only when security_review_status is 'waived', and forbidden otherwise. The minimum length exists to reject placeholders like 'n/a' or 'ok', which defeat the purpose of an auditable waiver.

waiver_timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the waiver was authorized. Required only when security_review_status is 'waived', and forbidden otherwise. Recorded separately from created_at so the audit trail shows when the exception was granted, which may precede the release record.

then.$comment: A waiver must be attributable, justified and timed.

else.$comment: Waiver fields are meaningless without a waiver, and their presence alongside 'passed' would misrepresent the record. Forbid rather than ignore.

$comment: Three rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are enforced by review instead (see .claude/agents/release-auditor.md): human_reviewer must differ from developer; rollback_safe must be false for a destructive migration; and waiver_authorized_by must actually hold the Technical Admin role.

examples.waiver_reason: Upstream advisory affects a dev-only dependency not present in the production build; tracked in issue #218.
